Kepler Communications is seeking an experienced Senior Electro-Optical/Infrared (EO/IR) Engineer to lead the make/buy strategy, design, assessment, trade studies, procurement, integration, and technical oversight of visible and infrared imaging payloads for space-based applications. The successful engineer understands the full signal chain, from photons to bits, and can engage the engineers and suppliers responsible for each key element of the payload.  
The role focuses on VNIR as well as cooled and uncooled infrared payloads that balance mission performance and product requirements against cost, schedule, and SWaP, and collaborates across Sales & Product, Satellite Systems Engineering, Hardware Engineering, Software Engineering & Perception, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and Test Engineering.

Key Responsibilities:: Payload Requirements, Interfaces, and Integration 
 Translate mission objectives and product requirements into EO/IR payload performance requirements, technical specifications, and enabling technologies, ensuring compatibility with spacecraft subsystems, software and perception needs, and operational architectures
 Establish key performance parameters, including operating wavelengths and spectral bands such as VNIR, SWIR, MWIR, LWIR, and multi-band options; ground sample distance and resolution; swath width; integration and readout time; noise-equivalent temperature difference (NETD); dynamic range; and radiometric accuracy and calibration
 Evaluate candidate payload architectures for SWaP, thermal, and spacecraft resource and margin impacts, as well as technology readiness, heritage, radiation tolerance, and launch-environment compatibility
 Own payload-to-spacecraft interfaces (electrical, mechanical, thermal, optical, and software), including interface control documents, working with internal hardware, systems, software, digital design, and perception teams to ensure the required electronics, image acquisition, and processing capabilities are in place 
 Optical, Spectral, and Radiometric Performance 
 Define and lead the optical design required for EO/IR payloads, including field-of-view selection, aperture sizing, focal length, and spectral filtering approaches, and review supplier optical designs
 Select and specify the appropriate telescope type and optical configuration (e.g., refractive, reflective, or catadioptric), applying geometric and diffraction optics principles to meet aperture, field-of-view, resolution, and spectral requirements
 Assess optical throughput, stray-light performance, and radiometric sensitivity; lead optical simulation reviews and performance verification 
 Integration, Calibration, and Test 
 Define payload qualification and acceptance criteria, including environmental test requirements, and review supplier performance and environmental test results
 Plan, conduct, and review EO/IR laboratory characterization across radiometric, spatial, spectral, and noise performance (e.g., NETD, SNR, MTF, MRTD, non-uniformity, and spectral response)
 Lead calibration planning, boresight alignment, image-quality verification, and payload integration readiness reviews
 Provide post-launch support, including on-orbit commissioning, performance assessment, and anomaly investigation and troubleshooting 
 Make/Buy Strategy and Trade Studies 
 Own Kepler’s make/buy strategy for EO/IR payloads and subsystems, weighing cost, investment, schedule, performance, risks, IP, and in-house capability; identify and develop relationships with strategic partners to support long-term payload capability
 Run trade studies on candidate detectors (cooled MCT, InSb, and T2SL; uncooled microbolometers; and emerging technologies), subsystems, and suppliers, assessing performance, maturity, exportability, supply-chain risk, cost, schedule, and space heritage 
 Vendor Evaluation and Procurement 
 Identify suppliers across optics, detectors, electronics, and back-end processing, and lead development of requests for information and requests for proposal
 Evaluate technical proposals, performance claims, compliance matrices, supplier capabilities, design maturity, review-gate readiness, and technical risks 
 Technical Ownership and Team Leadership 
 Own EO/IR payloads end to end, from concept definition through launch and on-orbit operations, identifying technical risks and driving mitigations
 Define the skill sets and key roles needed for future development, procurement, and integration of EO/IR payloads at Kepler, and help build the team required to advance capabilities in this domain

 Strong optical design and analysis expertise for visible and infrared imaging systems, including geometric and diffraction optics and telescope selection and specification
 Working knowledge of the end-to-end imaging chain, including detector physics, readout electronics, image processing, and onboard data handling
 Expert knowledge of EO/IR laboratory test techniques, covering the full range of imaging performance: radiometric (NETD, SNR, responsivity, dynamic range, linearity), spatial (MTF, PSF, MRTD), noise (temporal and fixed pattern), uniformity (non-uniformity correction, defective pixels), spectral response, and stray light; familiarity with cleanroom protocols is an asset

 À propos d’Abbott 
 Abbott est un chef de file mondial de l’industrie des soins de santé qui crée des solutions scientifiques révolutionnaires visant à améliorer la santé des gens. L’entreprise est résolument tournée vers l’avenir, à l’affût des changements qui pourraient survenir dans le domaine des sciences et des technologies médicales. 
 Être à l’emploi d’Abbott 
 En étant à l’emploi d’Abbott, vous pourrez faire un travail qui compte, vous perfectionner et apprendre, prendre soin de vous et des membres de votre famille, rester fidèle à ce que vous êtes et vivre pleinement. Vous pourrez : 
 • profiter de possibilités d’avancement professionnel au sein d’une entreprise internationale qui vous permettra de bâtir la carrière dont vous rêvez;
 • travailler pour une entreprise reconnue dans des douzaines de pays partout dans le monde comme étant un excellent milieu de travail et figurant parmi les entreprises les plus admirées dans le monde dans le classement Fortune;
 • travailler pour une grande entreprise reconnue comme étant l’une des meilleures où travailler, notamment pour ce qui a trait à la diversité du personnel, à la conciliation travail-famille ainsi qu’à la place des femmes dans les postes de cadres et les postes scientifiques. 
 L’occasion à saisir 
 Ce poste est basé à notre bureau à St-Laurent, au sein de la division Nutrition et nécessite une présence au bureau quatre jours par semaine, avec la possibilité de travailler à distance une journée.
 Le chef principal, Publicité numérique chez les détaillants, va diriger l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la stratégie auprès de nos principaux partenaires de vente au détail, comme Amazon Canada, Walmart Canada et Loblaw (PC Optimum/Advance).
 Ce poste se situe à la croisée du marketing, des ventes, du numérique et de la gestion de la relation client. Le titulaire du poste sera responsable de la stratégie globale d’expansion du commerce numérique, notamment de la publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants, de l’amélioration de la présence des produits en ligne et de l’optimisation du taux de conversions. Il devra assurer la performance du commerce numérique, en favorisant une croissance quantifiable et en renforçant la position d’Abbott en tant que chef de file de catégorie auprès des principaux détaillants.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Portée et retombées 
 • Gérer et optimiser un budget annuel de plusieurs millions de dollars destiné à la publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants et au commerce numérique sur diverses plateformes importantes
 • Influencer la planification commerciale conjointe et les stratégies de croissance de catégorie auprès des grands détaillants canadiens
 • Stimuler la performance du commerce numérique à toutes les étapes, allant de la génération de trafic à la conversion et aux achats répétés
 Équipe et méthode de travail 
 Travailler étroitement avec les équipes du Marketing, des Ventes et de la Gestion de la relation client, pour définir les priorités en matière de croissance, les plans d’action concertés et les objectifs commerciaux.
 • Collaborer avec des partenaires internes en analyses de données et en génération de constats (insights) afin de permettre la prise de décisions fondées sur des données et l’optimisation continue de la performance
 • Agir à titre de contact principal avec les équipes des États-Unis, afin de veiller à ce que nos méthodes concordent avec leurs stratégies, leurs meilleures pratiques et les initiatives mondiales, tout en étant adaptées aux besoins du marché canadien
 • Diriger et gérer le réseau d’agences externes, en étant responsable des relations avec les partenaires, en donnant des directives et en assurant une bonne exécution, tout en conservant un grand contrôle sur la stratégie à l’interne
 • Superviser toutes les étapes des projets de publicité chez les détaillants et de commerce numérique, en veillant au respect des délais et des normes de qualité, et à l’atteinte des objectifs
 • Servir d’intermédiaire principal entre les services concernés, en reliant les stratégies en matière de commerce, de médias et de clients pour favoriser une croissance cohérente et réplicable
 Principales responsabilités 
 • Être responsable de la stratégie commerciale et de la publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants
 • Diriger la stratégie de publicité sur les plateformes des détaillants et son exécution auprès d’Amazon Ads, de Walmart Connect et de Loblaw Advance
 • Assurer la performance du commerce numérique chez les principaux détaillants, afin de stimuler la croissance et la rentabilité.
 • Gérer l’allocation du budget, la stratégie d’enchères et l’optimisation de la performance afin de maximiser le rendement du capital investi
 • Définir et faire évoluer les champs lexicaux de mots-clés, les stratégies de ciblage et les plans de campagne
 • Gérer les agences externes tout en veillant à ce que l’orientation stratégique demeure à l’interne
 • Agir comme intermédiaire stratégique entre les équipes du Marketing, des Ventes et du Numérique
 • Établir de relations solides avec les détaillants afin de positionner Abbott comme chef de file de la croissance de catégorie
 • Contribuer à la stratégie de catégorie, à la stratégie de rayonnage et à l’accroche narrative de la vente au détail
 • Contribuer à la planification commerciale conjointe avec les grands détaillants, en profitant de leur potentiel de croissance
 Présence des produits en ligne 
 • Optimiser la présence des produits en ligne chez tous les détaillants : qualité des fiches produits, exactitude du contenu et conformité; référencement sur les plateformes des détaillants; notes, avis et leviers de conversion
 • Surveiller et optimiser le classement dans les résultats de recherche, le trafic vers les pages de produits, les taux de conversion, la disponibilité, les prix et l’assortiment
 • Soutenir le lancement et la gestion du cycle de vie des nouveaux produits (par exemple : configuration du produit dans le système, ventes aux détaillants, ventes aux consommateurs et disponibilité du produit)
 Analyses et mesures

Surveiller les indicateurs suivants : rendement des dépenses publicitaires, impact réel des campagnes publicitaires, acquisition de nouveaux clients et part de voix
 • Utiliser Profitero, Scintilla, Pacvue, LDIA, Springboard, Walmart Connect et Amazon Vendor Central pour analyser la concurrence et la présence des produits en ligne
 Intégration à la gestion de la relation client
 • Activer les segments ciblés dans le cadre de la gestion de la relation client sur les plateformes publicitaires des détaillants et chercher des moyens de participer à des programmes de fidélité
 • Apporter son soutien pour les déclencheurs de marketing du cycle de vie et les stratégies d’attribution
 • Mieux mesurer l’incidence des activités de gestion de la relation client sur les résultats des divers canaux commerciaux
 Compétences requises

 • De deux à trois ans d’expérience pratique avec les plateformes publicitaires des détaillants (p. ex. Amazon Ads, Walmart Connect et Loblaw Advance)

 • Excellente compréhension des méthodes permettant de mesurer l’impact réel des campagnes publicitaires et d’effectuer des tests A/B
 • Solide sens des affaires et excellente compréhension financière (budgétisation, prévisions et dépenses publicitaires)
 • Solides compétences en analyse et exploration de données

About Jetson 
 About Jetson 
 Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100M homes across North America away from burning fossil fuels to sustainable energy use. Here at Jetson, we believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.
 Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, which can be dramatically reduced by converting to heat pumps, however adoption lags due to high cost and friction in the retrofit process today. Solving one layer of the value chain won't move the needle on adoption. Mass adoption will come when it becomes a no-brainer for homeowners to transition. That is why Jetson is building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company. Jetson will make it simple, transparent, and affordable for everyone to get a heat pump.
 The Opportunity 
 Jetson is looking for a Community & Social Media Manager to own the relationship between Jetson and the people who live with our product.
 This is bigger than posting. You'll build the audience, and then you'll build the connection. The DMs, the comments, the Reddit threads, the group chats, the customers who love their heat pump and want to tell someone about it. You'll be the voice people hear when they reach out to Jetson, and the person who makes sure they hear back.

19f8354ea2:
You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter.
 Please read carefully: 
 1. Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What do you do for fun?
 3. Show us what you’ve done.
 Please include links to social accounts, campaigns, posts, videos, or other work you’ve helped create or manage.
 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.
 4. Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 We’re looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly and you can expect a prompt response.

 Job Description: 
 Primary Purpose   
 The Manager, Client Services and Operations, provides strategic oversight and day-to-day leadership of front-line client service operations. Reporting to the Campus Wellness Director and the University Medical Director, the Manager supports all units within Campus Wellness (Health Services, Specialized Care, Counselling Services and Health Promotion) to deliver effective, efficient, collaborative, and client-focused service. This includes supervising a team of Client Service Representatives (CSR’s) to optimize administrative workflows, communication and collaboration across various settings, and ensuring consistent adherence to privacy, accessibility, and service quality standards.   
 The Manager must maintain a thorough understanding of all front-line operations, systems, and processes, to ensure uninterrupted service delivery. They also serve as a key liaison between administrative and clinical teams, ensuring that client service operations are aligned with institutional priorities, regulatory requirements, and the evolving needs of the department.   
 Key Accountabilities   
 Strategic & Operational Leadership   
 Leads and continually improves the operations of client services, ensuring efficient and professional execution of day-to-day administrative functions.   
 Establishes clear expectations for client service standards that align with Campus Wellness’ mission and the University’s strategic goals of fostering a culture of excellence, equity and responsiveness.   
 Develops and implements standard operating procedures for client services that ensure an inclusive and welcoming experience for all individuals seeking information or services, reflecting the values of student-centered care and accessibility.   
 Ensures procedures, protocols and workflows are electronically documented, maintained and adhered to by the client service representatives to ensure consistency and accessibility across all Campus Wellness locations.   
 Collaborates with other Campus Wellness managers to improve coordination and collaboration across units, ensuring clear communication and streamlined operations.   
 Partners with Associate Directors of Health Services and Counselling Services to offer strategic input and administrative leadership on cross-functional initiatives and emerging priorities.   
 Ensures communication updates are shared with University of Waterloo communications team, particularly when information needs to be disseminated to students (e.g. clinic closures etc.).   
 Oversee the end-to-end workflow of client service representatives with the Electronic Health Records (EHR) system, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and efficiency.   
 Leads the implementation and optimization of clinical and administrative software systems, including end-user testing, workflow mapping, training, and troubleshooting.   
 Acts as the primary point of contact for technical support issues, coordinating with central IST teams to resolve system-related concerns, particularly with the EHR and integrated platforms.   
 Scheduling & Resource Optimization   
 Oversee the schedule creation of client service representatives, ensuring fair shift distribution, alignment with clinic hours, and compliance with employment standards and internal policies.   
 Manages consistent and equitable client service representative coverage across all Campus Wellness locations by developing and adjusting schedules based on operational needs, including client volume, staff absences, and emergencies.   
 Directs the input and optimization of provider schedules within the system, including configuring appointment types, booking preferences, and availability to ensure efficient, client-centered scheduling.   
 Proactively identifies and communicates gaps in provider coverage (e.g., intake specialists, triage specialists) to relevant managers and staff, providing data-driven recommendations to minimize disruptions.   
 Provides direction to client service representatives on rescheduling or canceling appointments due to clinic closures, absences, or other disruptions, and confirms affected clients are informed of alternate arrangements.   
 Monitors appointment utilization trends to assess scheduling efficiency and service capacity, providing feedback and recommendations to the Associate Directors and Directors to improve access and reduce waiting times.   
 People Leadership & Supervision   
 Leads the recruitment, onboarding, coaching and performance management of client service representative staff, aligning efforts with immediate operational needs and long-term workforce planning.   
 Establishes role clarity, accountability, and standard expectations of client service representatives to support consistent performance and client service delivery.   
 Fosters a respectful, inclusive, and psychologically safe workplace by modeling professional conduct, addressing conflicts through coaching and mentoring, and promoting collaboration and mutual respect.   
 Manages staff performance through a balanced approach, combining formal evaluations, informal feedback, one-on-one coaching, and developmental conversations.   
 Offers opportunities for professional development for team members, supporting continuous learning and career progression.   
 Champions professional growth by co-creating individualized performance goals, identifying learning opportunities, and guiding employees in building clear, achievable career pathways.   
 Ensures staff are equipped with the necessary tools, context, and information to perform their roles effectively, promoting autonomy, accountability, and confidence in decision-making.   
 Accountable for cross-training of client service representatives to guarantee operational flexibility and continuity of service.   
 Ensures client service representative compliance with privacy legislation (e.g., PHIPA, FIPPA) and confidentiality protocols, safeguarding client information across all systems and processes.   
 Trains and empowers client service representatives in identifying and escalating complex or high-risk client interactions, including those involving potential harm, while providing second-tier triage support and consulting with clinical staff as needed.   
 Enforces safety protocols to maintain a secure clinical environment, ensuring staff are current with required safety training and understand their responsibilities in maintaining a safe workplace.   
 Administrative Accounting Oversight   
 Oversee client payments for a range of healthcare related services (ex. forms and documents, verification of condition forms, pre-payment for services, non-insured immunizations, etc.), via variety of payment methods (ex. cash, credit, point of-sale terminals etc.); adhering to financial protocols and ensuring electronic and hard copy documentation accurately reflects services rendered and incoming payments.   
 Accountable for ensuring all financial transactions are accurate, reviewed for errors, and balanced at end of day.   
 Oversee client service representatives to ensure detailed and consistent documentation in EHR regarding changes in payment status, insurance, and decisions related to payment arrangements; make recommendations for improvement.   
 Manages the liaising between community in-patient care (GRH) and Campus Wellness clinical staff members (e.g. Associate Director, Clinical Case Manager, Mental Health Nurse) to ensure proper student insurance coverage or other methods for payment.   
 Oversee physician’s renumeration systems, including fee-for-service billings and direct payments to physicians from clients.   
 Process and maintain all WSIB claims seen by Campus Wellness providers; collaborate with the Health and Safety Office.   
 Collaboration & Strategic Partnerships   
 Builds and maintains strong, collaborative relationships within Campus Wellness, across university departments, and with community partners to ensure coordinated, student-centered service delivery.   
 Effectively communicates changes brought forward from Associate Directors to relevant team members in a timely and clear manner.   
 Contributes to Campus Wellness committees and initiatives by providing administrative leadership and operational insight that support continuous improvement and service excellence.   
 Provides leadership in planning and executing new Campus Wellness initiatives, ensuring timely completion, effective resource use, and alignment with departmental priorities.   
 Works with clinical staff to refine protocols for crisis response, ensuring administrative processes enable timely, coordinated, and compassionate support for students in distress.   
 Manages escalated concerns or complaints from faculty, clients, parents, and community members, resolving issues with professionalism, discretion, and a focus on service recovery.   
 Represents Campus Wellness as a knowledgeable and approachable liaison to the broader community, providing accurate, empathetic, and solutions-oriented support   
 Evaluation & Continuous Improvement   
 Leads the ongoing evaluation and improvement of systems and processes that impact client service, implementing enhancements that increase service quality, responsiveness, and operational efficiency.   
 Provides high-level oversight in the design, execution, and analysis of client feedback initiatives, integrating stakeholder insights into service planning and quality improvement efforts.   
 Presents data-driven analysis and reports on processes, workflows, and service metrics to inform evidence-based decision-making and resource allocation.   
 Serves as a change leader, guiding staff through organizational transitions, fostering adaptability, and supporting the successful adoption of new initiatives, technologies, and service models.   
 Required Qualifications   
 Education   
 University or College degree in Health Administration, Medical Administration, Business Administration, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and relevant management experience will also be considered.   
 Experience   
 At least five years of recent supervisory or management experience in a client service context.   
 Experience working in mental health and physical health care setting.   
 Demonstrated experience collaborating with other administrators at comparable and higher levels of responsibility.   
 Experience working with individuals from diverse accessibility, socioeconomic, and cultural backgrounds.   
 Experience managing staff and operational workflows while ensuring compliance with privacy/confidentiality legislation and institutional policies (e.g. PHIPA, FIPPA, professional regulatory requirements).   
 Knowledge/Skills/Abilities   
 Proven ability to lead, motivate, and support teams in a multi-disciplinary, client-focused environment.   
 Strong decision-making, problem-solving, and judgment skills, with the ability to resolve highly sensitive or confidential matters effectively.   
 Demonstrated collaboration, delegation, and leadership skills, with the flexibility to adapt leadership approach to different situations (e.g., collaborative, directive, supportive).   
 Extensive knowledge of Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems (Accuro preferred), MS Office suite, and SharePoint.   
 Ability to manage multiple priorities and competing demands while maintaining accuracy, discretion, and service quality.   
 Excellent oral and written communication skills, with professionalism, discretion, and the ability to effectively engage and influence stakeholders at all levels.   
 Knowledge of employment policies, supervisory best practices, and client service standards within a healthcare or wellness setting.

Positions are open to qualified candidates who are legally entitled to work in Canada.

 We pride ourselves on a culture of experimentation, accountability, and craft, continuously evolving how we design for conversion, engagement, retention, and long-term customer value.
 ABOUT THE ROLE
 In this role, you'll help our product designers move from intent to launch in more fluid, faster ways, while making sure everything we ship draws on the high-quality, evolving design language of our product. You'll do it by leading and evolving the design system foundations for Growth and the AI workflows that put them to work, making nuanced design judgment explicit and usable by both designers and AI agents. At times, you'll take point on larger cross-functional efforts, from new agent workflows to design-to-code. Our AI practice in design is still taking shape, and you'll be one of the people defining it.
 Our design system is the most important context our agents have. If it's unclear, so is everything they make. Get it right, and designers spend less time on production and handoff, and more time on the problems that matter most.
 A paramount part of this role is raising our craft bar. Growth ships more variants, states, and flows than any team can hand-build, and a single campaign can mean dozens of modals, emails, landing pages, and in-product flows. Speed can't come at the cost of quality: you'll define what excellent Growth design looks and feels like, establish clear guidance for when and why a designer or an agent should choose a particular pattern, and ensure every new experience strengthens a coherent system.
 Working closely with Product, Engineering, Content Design, Legal, and Data Science, you'll create a continuous learning loop between design principles, product experiences, evaluation, and evolving technology, shaping a system that becomes more capable and expressive as our experiences grow.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Find where designers lose time between intent and launch, such as production variants, handoff, and review, and design the system changes, agents, and workflows that remove it
 Set a high standard for craft and taste across Growth, and turn it into a clear, opinionated framework for when and how designers and agents should use each pattern, including the right default
 Own and evolve the foundations Growth is built on, including components, variants, tokens, layout, responsive behavior, and content and legal patterns, in partnership with our Design Systems team
 Establish a shared source of truth: a master Figma file of approved components, screens, and flows, connected to code through machine-readable specs that declare tokens, states, and edge cases
 Take point on building agents and skills that use the system to turn a request like "a renewal modal offering 14 days free" into on-brand, legally approved, production-ready design
 Translate design judgment into evals and review agents that check work before it ships, such as an agent that reviews designs against approved legal and content patterns, and use what they catch to improve the system
 Drive design-to-code efforts with Engineering, so agents can turn approved designs into shippable code that engineers review rather than rebuild
 Stay close to Growth work across incentives and lifecycle, spotting promising patterns and turning them into reusable, documented foundations every designer can adopt
 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
 7+ years of experience designing consumer-facing digital products across web and mobile
 A portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual, interaction, and product craft, including hands-on design system work
 Strong communication and storytelling skills, and comfort operating autonomously and carrying work from early concept through polished execution
 YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU
 Get energy from making other designers faster and better, and measure your impact by what the team ships
 Bring a high craft bar and are motivated to raise the quality, clarity, and distinctiveness of Growth design
 Have sophisticated design taste and can make the judgment behind it explicit, teachable, and actionable for designers and agents
 See a design system as a living body of product judgment, not simply a collection of components
 Have a strong command of interaction design, layout, content hierarchy, accessibility, and responsive behavior
 Can move fluently between foundational systems work and concrete, high-craft Growth experiences
 Care as much about choosing the right default as designing the full range of possibilities
 Can explain not only what a pattern should look like, but when a designer or an agent should choose it and why
 Are skilled at turning ambiguous or inconsistent work into a coherent, extensible system
 Are comfortable taking the lead on cross-functional efforts when the work calls for it, and bringing partners along
 Stay close to the latest AI developments, modern tooling, and component-driven design practices, and have built with agents, skills, or MCPs yourself
 We're looking for smart, curious designers who are excited to learn. This role spans craft, systems, and AI, and we don't expect anyone to match every line above. If the work excites you, we encourage you to apply.

About the Role
 You will be the person who makes our AI better at selling. You will read its conversations, notice what is working and what is not, and change the instructions it follows so the next thousand conversations go better.
 You do not need to know everything on day one. We will teach you our tools, our playbooks and how to write and test prompts. What we cannot teach is the instinct for conversations, a feel for sales, and the curiosity to dig into the data and ask why.
 What You'll Do
 Review AI-drafted text messages each day, and approve, edit or rewrite them before they send.
 Spot patterns across conversations, such as an opener that gets replies but no orders, and figure out the cause.
 Update each brand's prompts and playbook to fix problems at the source, then test the change before it goes live.
 Respond to brand requests and turn them into playbook updates.
 Help launch new brands: deep research on their brand, write the persona and opening messages, and check that offers work.
 Run and track A/B tests, and report what won. 
 You read people well. From one text you can tell whether a shopper is ready to buy, has a question, or is done, and you reply the way a real person would.
 You have sales instinct. You answer an objection and then ask for the sale, without arguing or pushing the customer away.
 You are curious about data. You can open a table of conversations and ask the right questions: how many, compared to what, at which brand, since when. You notice when a number looks off and go find out why.
 You fix the cause, not the symptom. When the AI says something wrong, you look for the reason (a missing fact, a vague rule, two rules that conflict) and fix the instruction so it does not happen again.
 You are comfortable with AI tools. You use ChatGPT, Claude or similar tools regularly and understand that how you ask shapes what you get back.

 Experience at a DTC brand or ecommerce agency.
 Familiarity with Shopify, Klaviyo, Postscript or similar tools.
 Spreadsheet skills, or basic SQL.
 Something you have built or automated with AI on your own.
 What We'll Teach You
 Our console, approval queue and playbook system.
 How to write, test and ship prompt changes.
 Shopify basics, discount codes and how they combine.
 How we run and read A/B tests.

We are building one of the most potentially consequential companies of the century. Our mission is to accelerate the world's transition to fusion energy while safeguarding humankind. This is not a normal company. This is not a normal job. We are committed for the long term to win.

As an Electrical Engineer at Fuse, you're building at the limit of what's possible, advancing pulsed-power technology as part of a team tackling the monumental challenge of fusion energy.




CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Design, build, and test control and data acquisition (DAQ) systems for pulsed-power facilities.

Design and assemble PCBs for control systems, diagnostics, and pulsed-power applications.

Diagnose, troubleshoot, and analyze the performance of electrical components, assemblies, and systems.

Develop control architectures spanning sensing, actuation, embedded hardware, and data acquisition.

Conduct applied R&D across electrical engineering, fusion energy, and pulsed-power systems.

Write specifications and technical reports and support systems through build, testing, and iteration.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent experience.

1+ years of experience in PCB schematic and layout design using Altium Designer or equivalent software.

1+ years of experience simulating electronic circuits using SPICE.

1+ years of experience designing control processes and control systems, including defining control architecture, sensing, and actuation.

1+ years of experience configuring and managing data acquisition (DAQ) systems.

Proficiency with lab equipment, including oscilloscopes, power supplies, and DMMs, as well as sensors and calibration techniques.

Experience with embedded hardware system design.

Ability and willingness to travel between Fuse locations as needed.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

C and/or Python programming ability.

Experience with pulsed-power, high-voltage, or high-current systems.

Familiarity with EMI hardening and protected I/O for electrically noisy environments.

Hands-on experience with embedded protocols such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, RS-485, or Ethernet.




WHAT WE VALUE

Give a shit. Build things you're proud of.

Take responsibility. If something is broken and you can fix it, fix it. See things through.

Move fast. Make decisions, learn quickly, and keep moving forward.

Think bigger. Simplify relentlessly. Don't default to the safe answer.

Disagree and commit. The best idea wins. Once a decision is made, we move.

Desire to win. This is hard. Expect intensity. We are here to win.

Plan B is to make Plan A work.




ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

Must be able to travel and work extended hours/weekends as needed.




BENEFITS

Medical, dental, and vision coverage.

Relocation assistance for roles that require it.

Flexible time off. Take what you need, no accrual tracking.

2 weeks of paid time off built into the end of each year, subject to team and business needs.

Supportive leave of absence policies.

Paid leave for new parents.





ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

 • Governance & compliance officer: Mandates, committee oversight, accountability, escalation, management information quality 
 • Policies & procedures: Currency, coverage of regulatory obligations, adherence, exceptions management 
 • Risk assessment: Enterprise and business-line risk assessment quality; customer risk rating model performance 
 • KYC / CDD / beneficial ownership: Identification, verification, BO and PEP/HIO determinations, third-party determinations, ongoing monitoring 
 • Enhanced due diligence: High-risk review timeliness and quality, backlog trends, demarketing decisions
